text.p: Argentine soccer star Diego Maradona, angry over apparent delays in obtaining a U.S. visa, denounced U.S. authorities Wednesday as "square-headed" and claimed that "nobody likes Americans."
The private news agency DyN reported Maradona was disappointed at having to wait to train in a special centre in Miami for his expected comeback after months of inactivity.

Maradona said Argentine President Carlos Menem, Argentina's ambassador to Washington, Raul Granillo Ocampo, and two former U.S. ambassadors to Argentina were trying to help him obtain the entry permit, DyN added.
U.S. embassy officials were unavailable for comment late Wednesday.

Maradona tested positive for drug use in the 1994 World Cup in the United States. He has been arrested for drug consumption and he acknowledges that despite treatment ordered by a judge he is still struggling to quit.
He agreed last month to return to play for Boca Juniors, Argentina's most popular team.
He said former U.S. Ambassador James Cheek became a fan of a local soccer club "to win people's hearts, as nobody likes Americans."
